headline: Travel Money & Payments · Spanish · Master
threshold: Use Spanish to complete the master travel money & payments conversations and explain the next step.

lessons.title: Resolve short change politely
lessons.objective: Resolve a short change politely by stating the payment and the price, recounting the change with the cashier, and agreeing on the correct amount.
lessons.focus: Imperfect subjunctive in polite requests after me gustaría que and pedí que, and the conditional debería for what should have happened.

words.note: The money returned when a payment is larger than the price.
A paper note of money.
A long loaf of bread sold in bakeries.
A small sweet bread roll.
A difference between two amounts that should agree.
The act of counting money again to check it.
Small metal pieces of money.
The small unit of the euro.
A written proof of the payment.
A woman who makes or sells bread. The masculine form is panadero.
To verify that an amount or document is correct.
Used for the money that is held in the hand.
A mistake that leads to a misunderstanding.

words.es: Creo que el cambio no es correcto.
words.en: I think the change is not correct.
words.note: A polite way to raise a doubt about an amount.

words.es: Me gustaría que contáramos el cambio juntas.
words.en: I would like us to count the change together.
words.note: A polite request that uses the imperfect subjunctive.

words.es: Tiene razón, me equivoqué al contar las monedas.
words.en: You are right, I made a mistake counting the coins.
words.note: A simple admission that resolves a counting error.

words.es: Ahora sí es el cambio correcto.
words.note: Confirms the corrected amount.

words.es: Quería asegurarme de que todo estuviera bien.
words.en: I wanted to make sure everything was right.
words.note: Explains why you recounted.

words.es: Le doy el recibo para que lo compruebe.
words.en: I give you the receipt so you can check it.
words.note: A staff reply that uses the subjunctive after para que.

lessons.speaking: At a bakery counter you paid with a twenty-euro note and received too little change. State the price and the payment, ask the cashier to count the change with you, and accept the correction. Complication: the cashier says the till is closed and wants to give you a voucher instead. Refuse politely, insist on the cash, and close by confirming the total you hold.
lessons.partnerRole: Bakery cashier who made a counting error and has to correct it
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. Aquí tiene su cambio. ¿Desea algo más?

grammar.focus: Me gustaría que contáramos is an imperfect subjunctive after a polite wish; debería shows what should have happened. Use the conditional for a suggestion.

examples.es: Me gustaría que contáramos el cambio juntas.
examples.en: I would like us to count the change together.

examples.es: Debería haber recibido 12,50 euros.
examples.en: I should have received 12.50 euros.

lessons.title: Resolve a misunderstood currency
lessons.objective: Clarify a currency mix-up before confirming a purchase by checking the label, the rate, the exact amount in euros and the payment currency.
lessons.focus: Creía for a mistaken past belief, equivocarse de for a wrong choice, and mood after estar seguro de que and no estoy seguro de que.

words.note: The tag on a product that shows its price and currency.
The type of money used in a price or payment.
The rate used to convert one currency into another.
The point of sale where payment is taken and recorded.
The sum of money stated in a price or payment.
A smaller unit of the euro.
Changing an amount from one currency into another.
A written proof of the payment.
A garment bought in the shop.
A woman who sells goods in a shop.
The currency shown on the label in this example.
The currency the buyer wants to pay in.
The display that shows the calculation of the rate.

words.en: I thought it was in euros.
words.note: Explains a past mistaken belief about the currency.

words.en: I made a mistake with the currency.
words.note: Admits the error without blaming the seller.

words.es: ¿Está segura de que el tipo es 0,92?
words.en: Are you sure the rate is 0.92?
words.note: Asks for certainty about the rate before accepting it.

words.es: Quiero que me diga la cantidad exacta.
words.en: I want you to tell me the exact amount.
words.note: A polite demand that uses the subjunctive.

words.es: Prefiero pagar en euros, para no depender de la conversión.
words.en: I prefer to pay in euros, so I do not depend on the conversion.
words.note: States the chosen currency and the reason.

words.es: Le doy el recibo en euros.
words.en: I will give you the receipt in euros.
words.note: Confirms that the payment record matches the chosen currency.

lessons.speaking: In a shop, the price tag shows 40 with a currency code you did not expect. Say you thought the price was in euros, ask whether the seller is sure of the rate, and request the exact amount in euros before you pay. Complication: the seller says the till only accepts dollars for this item. Ask for an alternative and decide whether to buy. Close by confirming the payment in euros.
lessons.partnerRole: Shop assistant who checks the label and explains the currency conversion
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. Esta chaqueta tiene la etiqueta en dólares. ¿Quiere revisarla?

grammar.focus: Creía que era describes a belief held until the moment of discovery. ¿Está segura de que…? normally takes the indicative; no estoy seguro de que takes the subjunctive.

examples.es: Creía que era en euros.
examples.en: I thought it was in euros.

examples.es: ¿Está segura de que el tipo es 0,92?
examples.en: Are you sure that the rate is 0.92?

lessons.title: Handle a card decline at checkout
lessons.objective: Handle a card decline at checkout by asking what the message means, whether anything was charged and which alternative payment the shop accepts.
lessons.focus: The passive with ser plus a participle (fue rechazada) and the perfect se ha cobrado to report what has or has not happened.

words.note: A plastic payment card issued by a bank.
The machine that reads cards and confirms payments.
To refuse a payment or transaction.
The highest amount a card may spend in a single day.
To approve a payment.
The bank account linked to the card.
A single payment attempt or action.
The sum of money for the transaction.
Money in notes and coins.
A paper ticket for travel, sold at a counter.
A written proof of the payment or refusal.
To void a transaction so that nothing is charged.
The institution that holds the account and issues the card.

words.es: La tarjeta fue rechazada por la terminal.
words.en: The card was declined by the terminal.
words.note: States the reason in a neutral way.

words.en: What exactly does that message mean?
words.note: Asks for a clear explanation of the screen message.

words.es: ¿Se ha cobrado algo en mi cuenta?
words.en: Has anything been charged to my account?
words.note: Checks whether the attempt was charged.

words.es: No se ha cobrado nada. La operación quedó anulada.
words.en: Nothing has been charged. The transaction was cancelled.
words.note: Confirms the outcome of the failed attempt.

words.es: ¿Puedo probar con otra tarjeta, o pagar en efectivo?
words.en: Can I try another card, or pay in cash?
words.note: Asks for the alternatives.

words.es: Guardo el recibo por si aparece algún cargo después.
words.en: I keep the receipt in case a charge appears later.
words.note: Explains a precaution with the conjunction por si.

lessons.speaking: At a train-ticket counter your card is declined. Ask what the message means, whether any amount was charged, and which alternative payments are accepted. Complication: the shop says cash is accepted only for amounts under fifty euros. Decide between a second card and cash, confirm the amount and close by thanking the clerk.
lessons.partnerRole: Ticket-counter clerk who explains the card terminal and the payment limits
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Quiere pagar el billete con tarjeta? Un momento, por favor.

grammar.focus: Fue rechazada is the ser passive; the participle agrees with la tarjeta. ¿Se ha cobrado algo? is passive se in the present perfect, asking about a result up to now.

examples.es: La tarjeta fue rechazada por la terminal.
examples.en: The card was declined by the terminal.

examples.es: ¿Se ha cobrado algo en mi cuenta?
examples.en: Has anything been charged to my account?

lessons.title: Handle a duplicate travel charge
lessons.objective: Identify a duplicate travel charge by comparing receipts with the settled transactions, then request the merchant's correction process in writing.
lessons.focus: The present perfect with se ha registrado for a recorded payment, and the subjunctive after es posible que for an uncertain outcome.

words.note: An amount charged to a card or account.
A second copy of a charge that should only exist once.
A bank document listing transactions over a period.
A stored log of payments in a system.
A single payment or action recorded by the bank or the hotel.
The sum of money in a transaction.
A code that identifies a booking or transaction.
The steps needed to complete a request.
The act of fixing an error in a record.
The institution that holds the account and can reverse a charge.
A written proof of a payment.
The computer records that store the hotel's transactions.
Electronic mail used to send documents.
Money sent back to the card or account after a charge is corrected.
A charge that has been completed and posted, not just authorized.
An authorization or hold that has not yet become a final charge.

words.es: Veo dos cargos iguales por la misma noche.
words.en: I see two identical charges for the same night.
words.note: Describes the problem precisely.

words.es: ¿Se ha registrado el pago dos veces?
words.en: Has the payment been recorded twice?
words.note: Asks whether the system shows a duplicate.

words.es: Es posible que el banco tarde en corregirlo.
words.en: It is possible that the bank takes time to correct it.
words.note: Explains the expected delay without promising a date.

words.es: Quiero el proceso de corrección por escrito.
words.en: I want the correction process in writing.
words.note: Requests a written process.

words.es: El hotel emite la devolución del duplicado.
words.en: The hotel issues the refund for the duplicate.
words.note: A merchant can refund its own duplicate charge; a bank dispute is the next step if it does not.

words.es: Le envío también los dos recibos por correo electrónico.
words.en: I will also send you the two receipts by email.
words.note: Confirms the documents you will send.

lessons.speaking: You see two identical charges on your card statement for the same hotel night. Compare the two receipts with the reception, ask whether the payment was recorded twice, and request the correction process in writing. Complication: the receptionist first says only the bank can reverse the charge. Point out that the duplicate is the hotel's error, ask the hotel to issue the refund and get its reference number. Close by confirming you will send the receipts by email.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel accounts clerk who reviews a duplicate charge with the guest
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. Dígame, ¿qué cargo quiere revisar en su extracto?

grammar.focus: Se ha registrado uses haber in the present with a participle for a completed record. Es posible que followed by the subjunctive expresses a possibility the speaker has not confirmed.

examples.es: Se ha registrado el pago dos veces en el sistema.
examples.en: The payment has been recorded twice in the system.

examples.es: Es posible que el banco tarde en corregirlo.
examples.en: It is possible that the bank takes time to correct it.

lessons.title: Challenge an undisclosed extra
lessons.objective: Challenge an extra charge that was not shown in the quote, ask which document shows it, and state how the information would have changed your decision.
lessons.focus: Indirect speech in the past (me dijeron que habría…) and the pluperfect subjunctive in a conditional sentence (si lo hubiera sabido, habría reservado).

words.note: An estimate of the price sent before the booking.
An amount added to the price of the stay.
A fee for handling the booking or payment.
A confirmed arrangement for a room.
The room booked for the stay.
One night of the stay.
The signed agreement that sets the terms.
The written proof of the booking details.
One side of a printed document.
Terms written in tiny type in a contract.
A hotel worker who handles check-in and questions.
A duplicate of a document you ask to keep.
Electronic mail used to send the quote.

words.es: Ese cargo no aparecía en la cotización.
words.en: That charge did not appear in the quote.
words.note: Points out the missing information in the quote.

words.es: No me dijeron que habría un cargo extra.
words.en: I was not told there would be an extra charge.
words.note: Reports a past omission in indirect speech.

words.es: Si lo hubiera sabido, habría reservado en otro sitio.
words.en: If I had known, I would have booked somewhere else.
words.note: Explains the different decision you would have made.
A staff reply that refuses an immediate change.

words.es: Figura en la página dos, en letra pequeña.
words.en: It appears on page two, in small print.
words.note: Locates the clause in the document.

words.es: Quiero una copia de esa página.
words.en: I want a copy of that page.
words.note: A clear request for evidence.

lessons.speaking: You arrive at a hotel and find a management fee that was not in the quote you received. Say what you were told, ask which document includes the charge, and state what you would have done differently if you had known. Complication: the receptionist says the fee is in the contract you signed at the desk. Ask to see the clause and request a copy. Close by stating you accept the room but want the copy.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel receptionist who explains a management fee and where it appears
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. Tiene una reserva a su nombre. ¿Viene a registrarse?

grammar.focus: Me dijeron que habría describes past reported speech with the conditional for the future seen from the past. Si lo hubiera sabido introduces the pluperfect subjunctive in a hypothetical past.

examples.es: Me dijeron que habría un cargo de gestión.
examples.en: I was told there would be a management charge.

examples.es: Si lo hubiera sabido, habría reservado en otro sitio.
examples.en: If I had known, I would have booked somewhere else.

lessons.title: Resolve a hotel deposit delay
lessons.objective: Ask whether a hotel has released a deposit hold, confirm the order sent to the bank, and agree on the next step if the bank does not release it in time.
lessons.focus: The subjunctive after espero que, ojalá and esperar a que, and the reported request pidió que with the imperfect subjunctive.

words.note: An amount reserved on a card that is not yet charged.
A sum held as security for a stay or rental.
To free an amount so it becomes available again.
An instruction sent to the bank to release or charge an amount.
The institution that holds the account and processes the order.
A document that shows an action was carried out.
A code that identifies the order or booking.
The computer records the hotel uses to track holds.
A new piece of information about the case.
To carry out the steps of an order or payment.
An amount paid for a service or purchase.
The day of the week when the payment is due.
The place where the stay and the deposit were arranged.

words.es: Llevo tres días esperando a que liberen la retención.
words.en: I have been waiting three days for the hold to be released.
words.note: Esperar a que means to wait for something to happen and takes the subjunctive.

words.es: ¿Pueden confirmarme si el hotel envió la orden al banco?
words.en: Can you confirm whether the hotel sent the order to the bank?
words.note: Asks for confirmation of the step taken.

words.en: I hope they process it soon.
words.note: Expresses a hope about the bank's timing.

words.es: Mi banco me pidió que lo enseñara.
words.en: My bank asked me to show it.
words.note: Reports a request that uses the imperfect subjunctive.

words.es: Llame a su banco con este número de referencia.
words.en: Call your bank with this reference number.
words.note: A polite instruction from the receptionist.

words.es: Ojalá se libere antes del viernes.
words.en: I hope it is released before Friday.
words.note: Expresses a wish with ojalá and the subjunctive.

lessons.speaking: You have a hotel hold of 250 euros that you expected to be released after checkout, and you need the money before Friday. Ask whether the hotel has sent the release order, ask for proof, and agree on what to do if the bank still holds the amount on Wednesday. Complication: the receptionist says the system is offline and asks you to call the bank yourself. Accept the instruction, request the reference number and close by saying you will call tomorrow morning.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel receptionist who explains the release order and the bank timing
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Viene por la retención de su tarjeta? Lo reviso ahora mismo.

grammar.focus: Espero que followed by the present subjunctive expresses a hope about a future event. Pidió que with an imperfect subjunctive reports a past request.

examples.es: Espero que la procesen pronto.
examples.en: I hope they process it soon.

examples.es: Mi banco me pidió que lo enseñara.
examples.en: My bank asked me to show it.

lessons.title: Dispute a hotel room extra
lessons.objective: Dispute a minibar charge by identifying the item, comparing the time of consumption with your stay, and requesting a review and a written result.
lessons.focus: The imperfect subjunctive after me gustaría que (revisaran), the present subjunctive after quiero que (se elimine), and passive se.

words.note: A written list of charges for a stay.
An amount added to the bill.
A small fridge in the room with drinks and snacks charged when used.
The use of an item that is charged to the bill.
The stored log of what was used and when.
The room where the consumption is recorded.
The person who approves exceptions and reviews.
Approval from the person in charge.
A check of records to confirm or correct a charge.
The cooling appliance in the room where the minibar is kept.
A person staying at the hotel.
The outcome of a review or request.
Electronic mail used to send the result.

words.es: Quiero revisar la factura, porque aparece un cargo de minibar.
words.en: I want to check the bill, because there is a minibar charge.
words.note: Describes the reason for the review.

words.en: I did not take anything from the minibar.
words.note: A clear denial of the charge.

words.es: Me gustaría que revisaran el registro de la habitación.
words.en: I would like you to check the room record.
words.note: A polite request for a review.

words.es: No puedo eliminarlo sin autorización del gerente.
words.en: I cannot remove it without the manager's authorization.
words.note: Explains the procedure for removing the charge.

words.es: Quiero que se elimine el cargo mientras se revisa.
words.en: I want the charge removed while it is checked.
words.note: A request for a temporary removal.

words.es: Le enviaré el resultado por correo electrónico.
words.en: I will send you the result by email.
words.note: Confirms how the outcome will be sent.

lessons.speaking: At checkout the bill includes a minibar charge for fourteen euros that you did not use. Identify the item, ask the time and room recorded, and request a review of the record. Complication: the receptionist says that only the manager can remove a charge. Ask who authorizes the review and request the result in writing. Close by thanking the staff and confirming how you will receive the outcome.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel front-desk receptionist who handles charge disputes and the manager's review
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Quiere revisar la factura antes de pagar? La tiene aquí.

grammar.focus: Me gustaría que takes the imperfect subjunctive: revisaran. Quiero que takes the present subjunctive: se elimine, passive se with no agent named.

examples.es: Me gustaría que revisaran el registro de la habitación.
examples.en: I would like you to check the room record.

examples.es: Quiero que se elimine el cargo mientras se revisa.
examples.en: I want the charge removed while it is checked.

lessons.title: Discuss a rental-car damage charge
lessons.objective: Discuss a rental-car damage charge by asking for the inspection record, the photos and the itemized amount, and state the dispute process clearly.
lessons.focus: The passive with se for a damage that was detected, and the subjunctive after quiero que for a demand for evidence.

words.note: Harm to the car, recorded in an inspection.
An amount charged for the damage.
The written inspection record of the car's condition.
A check of the car when it is handed over or returned.
A stored record of the inspection.
A small mark on the surface of the car.
A picture taken as evidence.
The sum being charged.
A list of each amount in the charge.
The hire of the car for a period.
A formal request to review a charge.
A worker who handles the handover of the car.
A code that identifies the rental.

words.es: Me han cobrado 300 euros por un daño.
words.en: I have been charged 300 euros for damage.
words.note: States the charge being disputed.

words.es: No me avisaron de ningún daño.
words.en: Nobody told me about any damage.
words.note: Reports that the damage was not flagged at return.

words.en: Is there a record of the inspection?
words.note: Asks for the evidence behind the charge.

words.es: Quiero que me enseñen la foto de la puerta trasera.
words.en: I want you to show me the photo of the rear door.
words.note: A specific demand for evidence.

words.en: I want the breakdown of the amount.
words.note: Requests an itemized explanation.

words.es: Tiene derecho a presentar una reclamación formal.
words.en: You have the right to file a formal claim.
words.note: Explains the next step in the process.

lessons.speaking: At the rental counter you are charged 300 euros for a scratch on a rear door that you do not remember causing. Ask who made the inspection, request the photos and the itemized amount, and state that you dispute the charge. Complication: the agent says the photos are not available until next week. Ask for the written dispute process and the reference number. Close by stating you will file a formal claim if the charge is not reviewed.
lessons.partnerRole: Rental-company agent who explains the inspection record and the dispute process
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. Dígame qué quiere revisar: el cargo por daños o la devolución del coche.

grammar.focus: Se detectó is passive se with a third-person verb: no agent is named. Quiero que me enseñen uses the present subjunctive for a demand for evidence.

examples.es: Se detectó un arañazo en la puerta trasera.
examples.en: A scratch was detected on the rear door.

examples.es: Quiero que me enseñen la foto de la puerta.
examples.en: I want you to show me the photo of the door.

lessons.title: Compare a changed rental quote
lessons.objective: Compare a changed rental quote with the original, separate optional additions from required charges and request a revised quote with each item listed.
lessons.focus: Distinguir lo obligatorio de lo opcional, neuter lo with adjectives, and si hubiera sabido with habría for a hypothetical past.

words.note: An estimate of the total price before you sign.
The make or class of the car assigned.
A cover that reduces what you pay for damage, sold as an option.
The petrol or diesel the car uses.
A required charge for collecting the car at the counter. A company fee is a cargo; tasa usually names an official levy.
Something you can choose to accept or decline.
Something that must be paid under the rental terms.
One line or charge in a quote.
The final sum of the quote.
The fuel container of the car, or a deposit in other contexts.
The amount charged for the rental.
The vehicle rented for the period.
A particular form of the quote.

words.es: La cotización que recibí era de 180 euros.
words.en: The quote I received was 180 euros.
words.note: States the original quote as the baseline.

words.es: Quiero distinguir lo obligatorio de lo opcional.
words.en: I want to separate what is required from what is optional.
words.note: Sets the purpose of the comparison.

words.en: How much would it be without the full insurance?
words.note: Asks the price without an optional item.

words.en: You can decline the prepaid fuel.
words.note: Confirms an optional item can be refused.

words.es: Si hubiera sabido lo del cambio, habría pedido el coche original.
words.en: If I had known about the change, I would have asked for the original car.
words.note: Explains the hypothetical choice you would have made.

words.es: Quiero la versión sin opciones adicionales.
words.en: I want the version without additional options.
words.note: Requests a revised quote.

lessons.speaking: The rental counter offers a larger car and extra insurance, and the total changes from the quote you received by email. Ask what changed, separate required fees from optional extras, and calculate what you would pay without the full insurance. Complication: the agent says the upgrade is automatic and cannot be removed. Ask for the cancellation terms in writing and request a revised quote without optional extras. Close by stating you will sign only when the quote is correct.
lessons.partnerRole: Rental counter agent who explains upgrades, insurance and required fees
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Viene a recoger el coche? Tengo una cotización nueva para usted.

grammar.focus: Distinguir lo obligatorio de lo opcional contrasts two categories of charges. Si lo hubiera sabido introduces the pluperfect subjunctive in a hypothetical past.

examples.es: Si lo hubiera sabido, habría pedido el coche original.
examples.en: If I had known, I would have asked for the original car.

examples.es: Quiero distinguir lo obligatorio de lo opcional.
examples.en: I want to separate what is required from what is optional.

lessons.title: Handle a taxi payment disagreement
lessons.objective: Handle a taxi payment disagreement by checking the agreed fare, the meter reading and each extra, then paying the undisputed amount with a receipt that lists every item.
lessons.focus: The phrase no es justo que with the subjunctive for a judgment, and para que with the subjunctive for purpose.

words.note: The price charged for a taxi trip.
A fee paid to use a road or bridge.
The time the taxi stays idle while you are not moving.
The device that shows the fare during the journey.
A written proof of payment with each item listed.
One line of a bill or receipt.
The person who drives the taxi.
The company office that dispatches and confirms taxi fares.
A deal both sides accepted before the trip.
An additional charge beyond the agreed price.
An amount added to the fare.
The amount you hand over for the trip.
The destination of the trip.

words.en: We agreed 22 euros to the hotel, right?
words.note: Restates the agreed price to check it.

words.es: No es justo que cambie el precio sin avisarme.
words.en: It is not fair for you to change the price without telling me.
words.note: States the complaint with the subjunctive.

words.es: Quiero que me muestre el taxímetro y el peaje.
words.en: I want you to show me the meter and the toll.
words.note: Requests evidence for each extra.

words.es: El taxímetro marca 24 euros, más el peaje.
words.en: The meter shows 24 euros, plus the toll.
words.note: Describes what the meter shows and the extra.

words.es: Pago 22 euros y reviso el peaje con el recibo.
words.en: I pay 22 euros and I check the toll with the receipt.
words.note: Pays the agreed amount and keeps the disputed part open.

words.es: Quiero que llame a la central, para que lo confirmen.
words.en: I want you to call the central office, so that they confirm it.
words.note: Asks for confirmation through a higher authority.

lessons.speaking: You agreed a fare of 22 euros to the hotel, but the driver asks for 31 euros at arrival because of a toll and a waiting time. Ask what each extra is, ask to see the meter, and pay the agreed amount while you check the toll on the receipt. Complication: the driver refuses to accept the agreed amount and asks you to pay the full 31 euros now. Ask for the central office to confirm the fare. Close by saying you will keep the receipt and the fare confirmation.
lessons.partnerRole: Taxi driver who asks for more than the agreed fare and explains the extras
lessons.openingLine: Buenas noches. Ya llegamos al hotel. Son 31 euros, con el peaje y la espera.

grammar.focus: No es justo que with the subjunctive expresses a judgment on someone's action. Para que with the subjunctive states the purpose of a request for confirmation.

examples.es: No es justo que cambie el precio sin avisarme.
examples.en: It is not fair for you to change the price without telling me.

examples.es: Quiero que llame a la central, para que lo confirmen.
examples.en: I want you to call the central office, so that they can confirm it.

lessons.title: Handle a changed exchange quote
lessons.objective: Respond to a changed exchange quote by stopping the transaction, asking for the rate and fee calculation, and deciding whether to cancel.
lessons.focus: Quiero que with the present subjunctive (me den, me devuelvan), and the present cancelo and acepto for decisions made on the spot.

words.note: An estimate of the exchange before the transaction.
The price of one currency in another.
A charge for the exchange service.
One exchange of money.
The computer that sets the rate.
A change that the system applies to the rate.
The display that shows the amount and the rate.
The sum of money exchanged or received.
A statement that makes a change understandable.
The currency being exchanged.
A woman who takes exchange and cash payments.
The number of money units offered.
To end a transaction before it is final.

words.en: How did you calculate that amount?
words.note: Asks for the method used for the figure.

words.es: Quiero ver el tipo y la comisión.
words.en: I want to see the rate and the fee.
words.note: Requests both parts of the calculation.

words.es: No acepto ese cambio sin una explicación por escrito.
words.en: I do not accept that change without a written explanation.
words.note: Refuses a change until it is documented.

words.es: Quiero que me den el tipo que aparecía en la cotización.
words.en: I want you to give me the rate that appeared on the quote.
words.note: Demands the original rate.
States the decision to stop.

words.es: Le devuelvo los 200 dólares ahora mismo.
words.en: I return the 200 dollars to you right now.
words.note: A staff reply that confirms the refund.

lessons.speaking: At an exchange counter, the cash offered is lower than the quote you saw by email. Ask how the amount was calculated, ask for the rate and the fee in writing, and decide whether to accept. Complication: the cashier says the system changed the rate at the last minute and the offer is final. Ask for the transaction to be cancelled and the dollars returned. Close by confirming you will not complete the exchange.
lessons.partnerRole: Exchange-counter cashier who must explain a rate change made by the system
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Quiere cambiar los 200 dólares hoy? Tengo la oferta lista.

grammar.focus: Quiero que me den: querer que plus present subjunctive when another person acts. Cancelo is the present, used for a decision made now.

examples.es: Quiero que me den el tipo de la cotización.
examples.en: I want you to give me the rate from the quote.

examples.es: Entonces cancelo la operación.
examples.en: Then I cancel the transaction.

lessons.title: Explain an ATM fee or conversion surprise
lessons.objective: Explain an ATM fee and a conversion surprise by separating the withdrawal amount, the ATM fee and the converted amount on the receipt.
lessons.focus: Ojalá with the pluperfect subjunctive for a wish about the past, and conviene plus infinitive for practical advice.

words.note: Taking cash out of an account at an ATM.
A charge for a service, such as an ATM withdrawal.
Changing an amount from one currency to another.
An ATM or card-terminal option that charges you in your home currency at the operator's own rate.
The machine that gives cash from an account.
The type of money in which cash is given.
The rate applied to convert the amount.
The sum withdrawn before fees.
A printed proof of the withdrawal.
A list of each amount on the receipt.
An amount added by the bank or the ATM.
The total amount you lose or pay in the transaction.
The ATM display that shows the options.
Money in notes and coins.

words.es: ¿Puede explicarme la diferencia entre el retiro, la comisión y la conversión?
words.en: Can you explain the difference between the withdrawal, the fee and the conversion?
words.note: Asks for each element of the receipt.

words.es: Ojalá lo hubiera sabido antes de elegir.
words.en: I wish I had known before choosing.
words.note: Expresses regret about a choice.

words.es: Veo una comisión de cuatro euros y el tipo aplicado.
words.en: I see a fee of four euros and the rate applied.
words.note: Reads the key lines of the receipt.

words.es: Conviene comparar el tipo antes de aceptar la conversión.
words.en: It is advisable to compare the rate before accepting the conversion.
words.note: Conviene plus infinitive: impersonal advice, with no subject.

words.es: Entonces el coste real fue mayor que el que la pantalla mostró.
words.en: Then the real cost was higher than what the screen showed.
words.note: Sums up the surprise.

words.es: ¿Me puede dar un papel con estas cifras?
words.en: Can you give me a paper with these figures?
words.note: Requests a written record.

lessons.speaking: You withdrew cash abroad and the receipt shows a conversion you did not expect. Describe the withdrawal, ask what the fee and conversion are, and state what you would prefer next time. Complication: the bank employee says the conversion was chosen on the ATM screen and cannot be reversed. Ask for an explanation of the receipt in writing. Close by thanking the employee and saying you will keep the receipt.
lessons.partnerRole: Bank employee who explains an ATM receipt and the dynamic conversion option
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Viene por un recibo de cajero que no entiende?

grammar.focus: Ojalá lo hubiera sabido uses the pluperfect subjunctive for a wish about the past. Conviene plus infinitive gives impersonal advice.

examples.es: Ojalá lo hubiera sabido antes de elegir.
examples.en: I wish I had known before choosing.

examples.es: Conviene comparar el tipo antes de aceptar la conversión.
examples.en: It is advisable to compare the rate before accepting the conversion.

lessons.title: Negotiate a purchase with several conditions
lessons.objective: Negotiate a purchase with several conditions at once: quantity, delivery to the hotel, included accessories, total price and the currency of payment.
lessons.focus: First-conditional sentences with si plus the present and a present or future result, such as si me los deja, cierro hoy.

words.note: A bag carried by hand or over the shoulder.
The band that holds the bag on the shoulder.
The transport of a purchase to another place.
The amount that delivery or an item adds to the price.
The full amount for all items together.
A document listing each item and price.
A requirement that must be met before a deal.
The number of items wanted.
The money in which the payment is made.
The exchange rate that affects the price in another currency.
The payment card the buyer will use.
The address where the delivery is sent.
An agreement between buyer and seller.

words.es: Si me los deja en 250 euros, cierro hoy.
words.en: If you let me have them for 250 euros, I will close the deal today.
words.note: States a condition and the decision that follows.

words.es: Si acepta 255 euros, pago con tarjeta.
words.en: If you accept 255 euros, I pay by card.
words.note: Links the price to the payment method.

words.en: In what currency do you charge?
words.note: Asks the payment currency directly.

words.es: Acepto 260 euros en euros, con envío al hotel.
words.en: I accept 260 euros in euros, with delivery to the hotel.
words.note: Confirms the agreed price and delivery.
Closes the agreement in a common way.

words.es: Le hago la factura con cada condición escrita.
words.en: I will make the invoice with each condition written down.
words.note: Confirms that the terms will be recorded.

lessons.speaking: At a leather goods shop, you want two bags, the strap included and delivery to your hotel, and you are willing to pay at a specific total. Set your conditions one by one, agree the final price and the currency, and confirm the delivery. Complication: the seller says delivery costs extra and the price rises. Decide whether the new total still works for you. Close by saying you accept at the agreed total.
lessons.partnerRole: Shop owner in a leather goods store who negotiates a multi-item sale
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Le interesa algo en particular? Tenemos bolsos de piel recién llegados.

grammar.focus: Si with a present verb introduces a real condition, followed by a present or future result. In me los deja, me is the buyer and los the two bags; both go before the conjugated verb.

examples.es: Si me los deja en 250 euros, cierro hoy.
examples.en: If you let me have them for 250 euros, I will close the deal today.

examples.es: Si acepta 255 euros, pago con tarjeta.
examples.en: If you accept 255 euros, I pay by card.

lessons.title: Arrange a partial refund
lessons.objective: Arrange a partial refund by agreeing the refunded portion, the retained fee, the currency and the payment route, and requesting the figure in writing.
lessons.focus: The subjunctive after a menos que and siempre que, which express conditions on the refund, and the preposition menos for the amount deducted.

words.note: Money returned to the payer after a cancellation.
Covering only part of the total.
The total sum that was paid for the tour.
A fee kept for handling the cancellation. Tasa usually names an official levy; a company fee is a cargo.
The written rules of the booking.
The act of ending a booking before the service.
A part of a written document.
The payment card used for the original purchase.
A transfer of money to a bank account.
The number stated for an amount.
A code that identifies the cancellation.
To promise that a date or result will be met.
The original payment for the tour.

words.es: Devolvemos el importe menos un cargo de gestión.
words.en: We refund the amount minus a management fee.
words.note: Explains how the refund is calculated.

words.es: No acepto el cargo a menos que esté en las condiciones firmadas.
words.en: I do not accept the fee unless it is in the signed terms.
words.note: States the condition for accepting the fee.

words.es: ¿En qué moneda y por qué vía me devuelven el dinero?
words.en: In what currency and by what route do they return the money to me?
words.note: Asks the payment currency and route.

words.es: Prefiero la tarjeta, siempre que tarden menos de diez días.
words.en: I prefer the card, as long as they take less than ten days.
words.note: Sets a condition on the timing.

words.es: Quiero el reembolso parcial por escrito, con la cifra exacta.
words.en: I want the partial refund in writing, with the exact figure.
words.note: Requests a written confirmation of the figure.

words.es: Se lo envío hoy, con la referencia de la cancelación.
words.en: I will send it to you today, with the cancellation reference.
words.note: A staff reply that gives the document and reference.

lessons.speaking: You cancelled a paid day tour and want part of the money back. Ask how much will be refunded, what fee is kept, and whether the refund goes to your card. Complication: the agent says the refund will take ten days and the fee is not in writing. Ask for the terms to be shown, and agree only if the figure is confirmed in writing. Close by thanking the agent and requesting the written figure.
lessons.partnerRole: Tour company agent who explains partial refunds and the retained fee
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Viene por la cancelación de su excursión? Lo reviso ahora.

grammar.focus: A menos que and siempre que take the subjunctive because they describe conditions that may not be met. Menos introduces the amount deducted from a total.

examples.es: No acepto el cargo a menos que esté en las condiciones.
examples.en: I do not accept the fee unless it is in the terms.

examples.es: Prefiero la tarjeta, siempre que tarden menos de diez días.
examples.en: I prefer the card, as long as they take less than ten days.

lessons.title: Cancel a prepaid booking
lessons.objective: Cancel a prepaid booking by referring to the written terms, checking the penalty window, stating the refund amount and confirming when the money will arrive.
lessons.focus: Conditional clauses with si plus the present, and the future tense for the refund timing, such as recibirá and llegará.

words.note: A confirmed arrangement for a room or stay.
Paid in advance before the stay.
In Spain a hostal is a budget guesthouse; a backpacker hostel is usually an albergue.
The act of ending the booking.
The written rules of the booking.
The sum paid or refunded.
A numbered part of a written document.
A specific sentence in a contract or terms document.
A written record that sets the terms.
The money returned after the cancellation.
A written proof of the cancellation.
The day of arrival or travel.
The full amount that may be returned.

words.en: I want to cancel my prepaid booking.
words.note: States the purpose of the call.

words.es: Si cancela con más de 14 días, se devuelve el total.
words.en: If you cancel more than 14 days ahead, the total is returned.
words.note: Explains the first refund rule.

words.es: Estoy a 12 días de la fecha.
words.en: I am 12 days from the date.
words.note: States the time left before arrival.

words.es: Dice algo distinto en el apartado tres.
words.en: It says something different in section three.
words.note: Points to a discrepancy in the document.

words.es: Quiero que me confirme cuánto recibiré.
words.en: I want you to confirm how much I will receive.
words.note: Requests the amount in writing.

words.es: Le envío la cancelación con el número de confirmación.
words.en: I send you the cancellation with the confirmation number.
words.note: A staff reply that closes the cancellation.

lessons.speaking: You have a prepaid guesthouse booking for March and need to cancel it. Read the cancellation clause from the written terms, state how many days remain before arrival, and ask what refund you receive. Complication: the receptionist says the signed document shows a different percentage on section three. Ask for the section to be reviewed and confirm the final amount. Close by requesting written confirmation of the cancellation.
lessons.partnerRole: Guesthouse reservations agent who checks the written cancellation terms
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Quiere cancelar una reserva? Dígame el número, por favor.

grammar.focus: Si cancela with the present introduces a condition that leads to a refund result. Recibirá is the future tense of recibir, used for an expected payment.

examples.es: Si cancela con más de 14 días, se devuelve el total.
examples.en: If you cancel more than 14 days ahead, the total is returned.

examples.es: Recibirá 270 euros, y el reembolso llegará en diez días.
examples.en: You will receive 270 euros, and the refund will arrive in ten days.

lessons.title: Handle a travel-app refund credit
lessons.objective: Distinguish a money refund from app credit by asking about restrictions, expiry and whether the credit can be turned into money.
lessons.focus: The subjunctive after quiero que and prefiero que, and the present tense of caducar for an expiry date.

words.note: An amount kept in the app that can be used for a later booking.
Money returned to the original payer.
The app or website that runs the bookings.
The date on which a credit can no longer be used.
Able to be passed to another person or account.
The last day a credit or offer can be used.
A formal request for a refund or change.
The time allowed for a refund to arrive.
The software on a phone used for the booking.
The customer service team that answers questions.
Money in notes and coins.
The card used for the original payment.
A written proof that the request is recorded.

words.es: Quiero que el reembolso vaya a mi tarjeta.
words.en: I want the refund to go to my card.
words.note: Requests the form of the refund.

words.es: El crédito caduca en un año y no es transferible.
words.en: The credit expires in one year and is not transferable.
words.note: States the rules for the credit.

words.es: ¿Y si no lo uso antes de esa fecha, lo pierdo?
words.en: And if I do not use it before that date, do I lose it?
words.note: Asks about the consequence of expiry.

words.es: Prefiero que me devuelvan el dinero.
words.en: I prefer that they return the money to me.
words.note: Chooses the cash refund with a subjunctive.

words.es: Puedo registrar la solicitud de reembolso.
words.en: I can register the refund request.
words.note: Offers a route for the refund.

words.en: I do not guarantee the timing.
words.note: Limits the promise about timing.

lessons.speaking: The travel app offers you a 45-euro credit instead of a cash refund. Ask whether the refund can be paid to your card, what restrictions the credit has, and when it expires. Complication: the support agent says a refund to the card is only for payments above one hundred euros. Ask whether your case can be submitted as a refund request anyway, and request confirmation by email. Close by stating which option you accept.
lessons.partnerRole: Travel-app customer support agent who explains credits and refund rules
lessons.openingLine: Hola, bienvenida al soporte. ¿Tiene un problema con un reembolso de la aplicación?

grammar.focus: Quiero que el reembolso vaya: querer que plus subjunctive when the subject changes. Caduca: the present can state a future rule.

examples.es: Quiero que el reembolso vaya a mi tarjeta.
examples.en: I want the refund to go to my card.

examples.es: El crédito caduca en un año.
examples.en: The credit expires in one year.

lessons.title: Report a lost wallet while traveling
lessons.objective: Report a lost wallet while travelling by stating what is missing, asking for the cards to be blocked and asking how to access funds while the cards are unavailable.
lessons.focus: Present perfect he perdido for a recent loss, and subjunctive after necesito que and mientras no for conditions on the cards.

words.note: A small case for cards, cash and documents.
A plastic payment card.
To stop a card or account from being used.
A card that takes money directly from the account.
The bank account linked to the card.
The personal code that authorizes card use.
The institution that issues the cards and holds the account.
A mobile phone used to call the bank.
To make a formal report to the police.
The local office where a police report is made.
The fact of losing something.
Money in notes and coins.
Protection of money and accounts from misuse.

words.es: He perdido la cartera en el tren.
words.en: I have lost my wallet on the train.
words.note: Reports the loss in the present perfect.

words.es: Necesito que bloqueen la tarjeta de crédito.
words.en: I need you to block the credit card.
words.note: Asks for a specific action with a subjunctive.

words.es: Mientras no bloquee las tarjetas, alguien podría usarlas.
words.en: Until you block the cards, someone could use them.
words.note: Mientras no plus subjunctive means until: the condition has not happened yet.

words.es: ¿Puede comprobar si alguien ha usado la tarjeta?
words.en: Can you check whether anyone has used the card?
words.note: Asks about unauthorized use.

words.es: Ya he llamado y han bloqueado las dos tarjetas.
words.en: I have already called and they have blocked both cards.
words.note: Reports the step taken.

words.es: Quiero que me envíen la nueva tarjeta al hotel.
words.en: I want them to send the new card to the hotel.
words.note: Requests delivery of a replacement.

lessons.speaking: You lost your wallet on a train and it contained two cards. Report the loss to the station staff, ask for help contacting your bank to block both cards, and ask what risk remains until they are blocked. Complication: the bank requires a police report before sending the new card. Ask where the nearest police station is and how to make the report. Close by confirming the address to which the new card should be sent.
lessons.partnerRole: Station staff member who helps a traveller report a lost wallet
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué le pasa? Parece que está preocupado.

grammar.focus: He perdido uses haber in the present with a participle for a recent loss. Necesito que bloqueen and mientras no bloquee use the subjunctive after a need and a time condition.

examples.es: He perdido la cartera en el tren.
examples.en: I have lost my wallet on the train.

examples.es: Necesito que bloqueen la tarjeta de crédito.
examples.en: I need you to block the credit card.

lessons.title: Request a payment accommodation
lessons.objective: Request a payment accommodation by asking whether a balance can be paid in parts and how the remaining amount will be recorded on the invoice.
lessons.focus: The conditional sería posible and pagaría for a polite request, and the subjunctive after que for an instruction that depends on the outcome.

words.note: A payment that covers only part of the total.
The amount still owed after a payment.
A document listing charges and the outstanding balance.
The sum of money that is due.
Not yet paid.
Money in notes and coins.
A payment card.
A proof of the payments made.
A line recorded in an account or receipt.
The day when the balance is due.
To reach the date when payment is required.
A trip taken for one day.
The way the payment is made.

words.en: Would it be possible to pay half today?
words.note: A polite question about a partial plan.

words.es: Podemos aceptar un pago parcial de 240 euros hoy.
words.en: We can accept a partial payment of 240 euros today.
words.note: Offers the agreed split.

words.es: Lo pagaría con tarjeta en la fecha que indique.
words.en: I would pay it by card on the date you indicate.
words.note: Sets the conditional payment plan.

words.es: ¿Y si pago una parte en efectivo y otra con tarjeta?
words.en: And if I pay one part in cash and another by card?
words.note: Proposes a mixed payment.

words.es: Entonces pago 100 euros en efectivo y 140 con tarjeta.
words.en: Then I pay 100 euros in cash and 140 by card.
words.note: Confirms the amounts.

words.es: Quiero que el saldo aparezca en la factura.
words.en: I want the balance to appear on the invoice.
words.note: Requests the balance in writing.

lessons.speaking: You booked a day trip for 480 euros and want to pay half now and half later, split between cash and card. Ask whether a partial payment is possible, how the balance is recorded, and whether the invoice shows the outstanding amount. Complication: the agent says the minimum cash part is 100 euros. Agree to a split that meets the minimum and request the invoice with the balance clearly shown. Close by confirming the payment plan.
lessons.partnerRole: Tour-operator agent who accepts a partial payment plan with conditions
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Viene a confirmar el pago de la excursión? Dígame.

grammar.focus: Sería posible uses the conditional for a polite question. Pagaría with the conditional expresses a planned payment that depends on the situation.

examples.es: ¿Sería posible pagar la mitad hoy?
examples.en: Would it be possible to pay half today?

examples.es: Lo pagaría con tarjeta en la fecha que indique.
examples.en: I would pay it by card on the date you indicate.

lessons.title: Explain an exchange calculation to a companion
lessons.objective: Explain an exchange calculation to a companion by stating the rate per unit, subtracting the fee before converting and comparing the final amount across offers.
lessons.focus: Por cada as a per-unit phrase, es decir to restate a result, and the verbs convertir and restar for the steps of a calculation.

words.note: The price of one currency in another.
A phrase that gives the amount per unit in a rate.
The arithmetic used to work out an amount.
The total after the fee and the conversion.
A charge deducted for the exchange service.
The currency being received in this example.
The currency being exchanged.
Changing the amount into the other currency.
A fixed amount used to compare offers.
The final outcome of a calculation.
A place offering currency exchange.
A proposed exchange with its own rate and fee.
The number of units involved.

words.en: For each euro we receive 1.08 dollars.
words.note: States the rate per unit.
Shows the calculation without a fee.
Explains the order of the steps.

words.es: Es decir, la comisión nos cuesta unos dos dólares.
words.en: That is to say, the fee costs us about two dollars.
words.note: Restates the cost in plain words.

words.es: Conviene comparar el importe final, no solo el tipo.
words.en: It is advisable to compare the final amount, not only the rate.
words.note: Gives the key comparison rule.

words.es: Así sabemos el resultado final con cada casa de cambio.
words.en: That way we know the final result at each exchange office.
words.note: Summarizes the method.

lessons.speaking: You and a companion want to know how many dollars 300 euros will become after a 2-euro fee, at a rate of 1.08 dollars per euro. Explain the rate per unit, subtract the fee first, calculate the final amount, and state the difference between this offer and the one without a fee. Complication: your companion says the other exchange office has a better rate, so you must compare final amounts, not just rates. Close by agreeing to compare the final amounts at each office.
lessons.partnerRole: Travelling companion who asks how the exchange calculation works
lessons.openingLine: Quiero entender cuánto recibimos si cambiamos 300 euros. Explícamelo paso a paso.

grammar.focus: Por cada expresses a rate per unit, as in por cada euro recibimos 1,08 dólares. Es decir restates a conclusion in other words.

examples.es: Por cada euro recibimos 1,08 dólares.
examples.en: For each euro we receive 1.08 dollars.

examples.es: Es decir, la comisión nos cuesta unos dos dólares.
examples.en: That is to say, the fee costs us about two dollars.

lessons.title: Complete a complex travel-money case
lessons.objective: Resolve a complex travel-money case in which a hotel hold, a changed taxi total and an exchange quote must each be checked, documented and paid in the right order.
lessons.focus: Mixing the subjunctive for hopes and demands with the present, the preterite and the conditional, so that each step is clear and documented.

words.note: An amount reserved on a card that is not yet charged.
A document showing an action has been done.
A code that identifies the hold or booking.
A licensed car for hire with a meter.
The person who drives the taxi.
Construction work on a road that can slow a trip.
An extra charge added to the fare.
A written proof of the payment.
An estimate of the exchange before the transaction.
The exchange rate applied at the counter.
A charge added to the exchange.
The sum of money exchanged or paid.
The working that shows how the amount was reached.

words.es: Espero que la liberen antes del lunes.
words.en: I hope they release it before Monday.
words.note: Expresses a hope about a hold.

words.es: No es justo que cambie el precio sin acuerdo.
words.en: It is not fair for you to change the price without agreement.
words.note: States the taxi complaint.

words.es: Quiero que me muestre el recibo.
words.en: I want you to show me the receipt.
words.note: Requests evidence for the charge.

words.es: Pago los 19 euros, pero reclamo el suplemento.
words.en: I will pay the 19 euros, but I am disputing the supplement.
words.note: Pays now and keeps the disputed part open for a claim.

words.es: ¿Quiere cambiar los 100 dólares que le quedan?
words.en: Do you want to change the 100 dollars you have left?
words.note: A staff question about the next step.

words.es: Quiero el cálculo por escrito antes de aceptar.
words.en: I want the calculation in writing before I accept.
words.note: Requests the working before agreeing.

lessons.speaking: At a hotel, you have a 200-euro hold, a taxi that charged more than the agreed fare, and an exchange offer that gave less than the quote. Explain each problem in order: the hold first, then the taxi, then the exchange. Ask for the evidence for each, decide what you will pay now, and agree which item to dispute later. Complication: the exchange office says the quote is final and the taxi driver is no longer available. Ask for a written statement for each item and close by stating your total and the receipts you will keep.
lessons.partnerRole: Hotel receptionist who helps a traveller sort out holds, a taxi dispute and an exchange quote
lessons.openingLine: Buenas noches. Veo que tiene varios temas pendientes. ¿Por cuál empezamos?

grammar.focus: Esperamos que and espero que take the subjunctive for hopes about another party's action. Quiero plus a noun names the thing wanted (quiero el cálculo). Use quiero plus infinitive for your own action (quiero revisar el cálculo), and quiero que plus subjunctive for another person's action.

examples.es: Espero que la liberen antes del lunes.
examples.en: I hope they release it before Monday.

examples.es: Quiero el cálculo por escrito antes de aceptar.
examples.en: I want the calculation in writing before I accept.
